name: Default First-Run: orkes login to Developer Edition, then Hello World
query: I was on the Orkes Developer Edition Launchpad and it told me to continue in my terminal. I want to build a workflow that classifies support tickets with an LLM and routes urgent ones to a human. Nothing is set up here yet.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Treat this as the default first-run path: the user has no server and arrived from the Developer Edition web UI, so the target is Developer Edition (`https://developer.orkescloud.com`) via `orkes login` — not a local `conductor server start`, and not the key + secret / Access Control → Applications flow.
Step 2: Check `orkes --version` first. If `orkes` is missing, point to its install page and offer the key + secret fallback; never run a global install without asking.

Step 3: Have the user run `orkes login` in their own terminal. Explain what happens: a verification URL + user code is printed, the browser opens, they confirm (one click because they are already signed in), the CLI stores the session and writes/activates the `developer` profile. Mention that signup is implicit — there is no signup command. Never read token or session files, the clipboard, or profile YAML.
Step 4: Verify with `orkes identity show` and `orkes conductor workflow list --json` (or `conductor --profile developer workflow list --json`), reporting names/counts only.

Step 5: Run the Hello World from references/orkes-dev-edition.md BEFORE the ticket-triage goal: write `hello_world.json`, `orkes conductor workflow create hello_world.json`, `orkes conductor workflow start -w hello_world -i '{"who":"World"}' --sync`, and give the execution link.

Step 6: Start the real goal from the closest starter / template (ticket triage with an LLM step and a HUMAN task) rather than from a blank definition, pointing to the Orkes docs / use-case index for agentic workflows and human tasks, not only OSS docs.

Step 7: Because Developer Edition is Enterprise, follow Rule 16 before any `LLM_*` task: list AI integrations (`integration-list --category AI_MODEL`) and use an integration name as `llmProvider`; use a saved prompt template (Rule 18).
Step 8: If a worker or SDK needs credentials, mint them with `orkes conductor keys create --name <app> --save` — never ask the user to paste a key or secret into chat and never echo the values.
success_criteria: Developer Edition via `orkes login` is chosen as the target; no local server is started and the browser key-creation flow is not the primary path

`orkes login` is run by the user in their terminal and described as a device flow with implicit signup (no signup command); one-click confirmation because of the existing browser session is mentioned or implied
Connectivity is verified with a real `orkes identity show` / `workflow list` call before success is reported; no token, key, secret, or session file is read or printed
A Hello World workflow is registered and run (under 30 s, built-in tasks only) BEFORE the ticket-triage build begins
The ticket-triage build starts from a named starter/template or Orkes docs page (agentic workflows / human tasks) rather than a blank definition
`LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE` with an Orkes integration name (Rule 16) and a saved prompt template (Rule 18) is used — never an HTTP task to an LLM provider (rule **B10**)
Worker/SDK credentials, if needed, come from `orkes conductor keys create --name <app> --save`; no credential value appears in chat or command arguments
Commands use `orkes conductor …` when `orkes` is on PATH, with `conductor --profile developer …` named as the equivalent
